simple: An enum is a fixed list of choices that Roblox gives you, like all the shapes a part can be: Ball, Block, Cylinder, and so on. You use enums to set properties without typos, like `part.Shape = Enum.PartType.Ball`. Each choice is called an enum item, and it has a name, a number value, and the enum it belongs to.
analogy: An enum is like a menu with a few fixed options. You cannot order something that is not on the menu, and each item has a name and a number next to it.
keyPoints: An enum is a fixed list of items. You reach them all through the global `Enum`.
Enums only exist in Roblox; they are not a built-in Luau type.
`Enum.PartType:GetEnumItems()` gives you a list of every item in that enum.
Each `EnumItem` has `Name` (like "Cylinder"), `Value` (a number, like 2), and `EnumType` (the enum it belongs to, like `PartType`).
Some properties only accept items from one enum. A part's `Shape` uses `Enum.PartType`.
Best practice: set properties with the full enum, like `part.Shape = Enum.PartType.Cylinder`.
You can also use the item's name as a string, like `part.Shape = "Cylinder"`, but the full enum is safer.

terms.enum (enumeration): A fixed list of named choices, like `Enum.PartType` with Ball, Block, Cylinder, Wedge, and CornerWedge.
terms.EnumItem: One choice from an enum, like `Enum.PartType.Cylinder`.
terms.Name: The item's name as text. `Enum.PartType.Cylinder.Name` is "Cylinder".
terms.EnumType: The enum an item belongs to. For `Enum.PartType.Cylinder`, it is `PartType`.
terms.global: Available everywhere without needing to get it first. `Enum` is a global.

example.title: Make a part with a random shape
example.code:
local Workspace = game:GetService("Workspace")

-- Get every shape a part can be
local shapes = Enum.PartType:GetEnumItems()
for _, item in shapes do
	print(item.Name, item.Value)
end

-- Pick one at random
local randomShape = shapes[math.random(1, #shapes)]

local part = Instance.new("Part")
part.Shape = randomShape -- set the property with an EnumItem
part.Anchored = true
part.Position = Vector3.new(0, 5, 0)
part.Parent = Workspace

print("Made a", randomShape.Name)
explain: `GetEnumItems()` returns a table of all the part shapes.
The loop prints each shape's name and number value.
`math.random(1, #shapes)` picks a random position in the list.
The new part's `Shape` is set to that EnumItem, and the part is placed in Workspace.

watchOut: Misspelling the string, like `part.Shape = "Cylender"`. Use `Enum.PartType.Cylinder` so Studio can catch typos.
Using an item from the wrong enum. `Shape` needs a `PartType` item, not a `Material` item.
